llm.summary: This browser automation skill is mostly transparent, but its guidance conflicts on when to re-check the page before acting, which matters because it can operate on logged-in sites and session data.

dimensions.detail: The local daemon binds to 127.0.0.1 and uses a random token, safe mode, visible browser windows, idle auto-exit, and path confinement, but the default full mode remains broad browser authority intended only for trusted local use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a Node package using playwright-core only, with no bundled node_modules and no browser-download install path shown; the wrapper script just sets NODE_PATH and runs pw-browser.js.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md first says agents must run a fresh snap before every interaction, but later says stable refs mean agents need not re-snap every step and recommends batching actions; that ambiguity can make stale references more likely during real authenticated browser actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent daemon state and cookie/localStorage export/import are explicit and purpose-aligned, with mitigations such as PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE, PW_BROWSER_CRED_PERSIST=off, 0700/0600 file permissions, confined credential paths, and operator-gated unsafe path override.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a Playwright browser automation CLI, and the high-impact abilities are openly described: page JavaScript execution, daemon-side Playwright code, cookie/localStorage read-write, downloads/uploads, and persistent browser state.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for trusted, local, user-visible browser automation. Use PW_BROWSER_SAFE_MODE=1 for semi-trusted agents or untrusted inputs, and PW_BROWSER_CRED_PERSIST=off when session files should never be written. Treat exported cookies/localStorage as passwords, delete them when done, and require a fresh snap whenever a page may have changed despite the stable-ref optimization text.
llm.findings:
[SDI-4] unexpected: The scanner's concern is supported: line-level review confirms contradictory snap guidance in SKILL.md, and this is material because click/fill actions use cached refs when no fresh snap is taken.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The token-saving advice to reuse refs and batch actions is not inherently unsafe, but as written it weakens the earlier mandatory observe-before-act rule without clearly limiting reuse to stable pages or the self-correcting act flow.
[RA2] expected: Cookie and localStorage export/import are real session-persistence capabilities, but they are prominently disclosed, documented as risky, confined by default, and can be disabled by operator-controlled environment settings.
